```odin
import rt "fire:rt"
```

Realtime-thread utilities. Everything here is [rt]-safe unless noted.

## Constants

### CACHE_LINE

```odin
CACHE_LINE :: 64
```

Assumed cache line size in bytes, used to pad shared atomics apart and
avoid false sharing.

## Types

### Mpmc_Queue

```odin
Mpmc_Queue :: struct {
}
```

Bounded lock-free multi-producer / multi-consumer queue (Vyukov's design:
each cell carries a sequence number saying whose turn it is). Any thread
may push and pop. Capacity is rounded up to a power of two.

### FP_State

```odin
FP_State :: u64
```

Saved floating-point control register state, returned by
`enable_flush_to_zero` and passed back to `restore_fp_state`.

### Spsc_Queue

```odin
Spsc_Queue :: struct {
}
```

Bounded lock-free single-producer / single-consumer queue.
Exactly one thread may push and exactly one (other) thread may pop.
Capacity is rounded up to a power of two.

## Procedures

### host_time_ns

```odin
host_time_ns :: proc "contextless"() -> u64
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). The clock all device and MIDI timestamps use, in nanoseconds from an
arbitrary origin. On macOS it is mach_absolute_time (CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW), the
clock CoreAudio and CoreMIDI timestamps use; it stops while the machine
sleeps (unlike CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW, which core:time uses there). Elsewhere it
is core:time's monotonic tick (QueryPerformanceCounter on Windows, which
WASAPI timestamps use).

### mpmc_init

```odin
mpmc_init :: proc(q: ^Mpmc_Queue($T), capacity: int, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> runtime.Allocator_Error
```

Control thread. Allocates room for at least `capacity` items (rounded up to
a power of two, minimum 2) with `allocator`. Free with `mpmc_destroy`.

### mpmc_destroy

```odin
mpmc_destroy :: proc(q: ^Mpmc_Queue($T), allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator)
```

Control thread. Frees the cells; pass the allocator given to `mpmc_init`.
No thread may use the queue afterwards.

### mpmc_push

```odin
mpmc_push :: proc "contextless"(q: ^Mpmc_Queue($T), value: T) -> bool
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Any thread. Copies `value` in; returns false (and drops it) if full.
Lock-free: may retry under contention but never blocks.

### mpmc_pop

```odin
mpmc_pop :: proc "contextless"(q: ^Mpmc_Queue($T)) -> (value: T, ok: bool)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Any thread. Takes the oldest value; returns false if empty.
Lock-free: may retry under contention but never blocks.

### mpmc_capacity

```odin
mpmc_capacity :: proc "contextless"(q: ^Mpmc_Queue($T)) -> int
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Maximum number of items the queue holds (the rounded-up capacity).

### set_realtime_priority

```odin
set_realtime_priority :: proc(priority: int = 80, period_ns: u64 = 0) -> bool
```

Gives the calling thread realtime scheduling. Call it from the thread
itself, before it starts processing; returns false if the OS refused (the
thread then keeps normal priority).

- macOS: a Mach time-constraint policy, as CoreAudio uses for its IO
  thread: the thread wants half of `period_ns` (one audio block; 0 means
  2.9 ms) in every `period_ns`. No privileges needed.
- Linux: SCHED_FIFO at `priority` (1–99; JACK and PipeWire use 70–90).
  Needs CAP_SYS_NICE or an rtprio limit (/etc/security/limits.d).
- Windows: MMCSS "Pro Audio", as WASAPI audio threads use, for the
  thread's lifetime.
- Elsewhere: not supported (returns false).

### enable_flush_to_zero

```odin
enable_flush_to_zero :: proc "contextless"() -> FP_State
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Enable flush-to-zero (and denormals-are-zero on x86) for the calling
thread. Returns the previous state so it can be restored.

### restore_fp_state

```odin
restore_fp_state :: proc "contextless"(s: FP_State)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Restores the calling thread's floating-point control state saved by
`enable_flush_to_zero`.

### flush_to_zero_enabled

```odin
flush_to_zero_enabled :: proc "contextless"() -> bool
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Reports whether flush-to-zero (and DAZ on x86) is on for the calling
thread. Always false on architectures without support.

### precise_sleep

```odin
precise_sleep :: proc(d: time.Duration)
```

Sleeps for `d` with sub-millisecond precision, without spinning: nanosleep,
or on Windows a high-resolution waitable timer (time.sleep there rounds down
to whole milliseconds, and Sleep(0) only yields). Not for the audio thread.

### spsc_init

```odin
spsc_init :: proc(q: ^Spsc_Queue($T), capacity: int, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> runtime.Allocator_Error
```

Control thread. Allocates room for at least `capacity` items (rounded up to
a power of two) with `allocator`. Free with `spsc_destroy`.

### spsc_destroy

```odin
spsc_destroy :: proc(q: ^Spsc_Queue($T), allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator)
```

Control thread. Frees the buffer; pass the allocator given to `spsc_init`.
Neither endpoint may use the queue afterwards.

### spsc_push

```odin
spsc_push :: proc "contextless"(q: ^Spsc_Queue($T), value: T) -> bool
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Producer side. Copies `value` in; returns false (and drops it) if full.

### spsc_pop

```odin
spsc_pop :: proc "contextless"(q: ^Spsc_Queue($T)) -> (value: T, ok: bool)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Consumer side. Takes the oldest value; returns false if empty.

### spsc_len

```odin
spsc_len :: proc "contextless"(q: ^Spsc_Queue($T)) -> int
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Number of queued items. Approximate; exact only when called from
either endpoint thread.

### spsc_capacity

```odin
spsc_capacity :: proc "contextless"(q: ^Spsc_Queue($T)) -> int
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Maximum number of items the queue holds (the rounded-up capacity).
